<!-- SOURCE_TURN_007_BEGIN -->
It's true that the amount of information available online can be overwhelming, and it's humanly impossible to keep up with everything that's going on every time. Social media platforms are designed to generate vast amounts of content, and the algorithms are such that they ensure users are always engaged.

One thing that you can do to make sure you stay informed without getting overwhelmed is to practice critical thinking and prioritize reliable sources over sensational ones. It's also essential to take breaks from consuming information and to be mindful of the information you take in. Consider taking time to verify sources and information, double-check the credibility of the author or publisher, and seek multiple sources to compare and contrast ideas.

Furthermore, it would help to follow publications and journalists that you trust while understanding their biases, and this will help you keep the noise down and develop a healthy media diet. Also, be wary of echo chambers and consider expanding your sources beyond your usual scope to get a broader perspective.

Therefore, finding a balance between staying informed and taking outlets to ensure that the information consumed is factual, reliable, and doesn't trigger anxiety is essential.
<!-- SOURCE_TURN_007_END -->

<!-- SOURCE_TURN_009_BEGIN -->
It's understandable that trying to verify every piece of information can be exhausting, and it's easy to feel overwhelmed. However, there are several ways to stay informed while also avoiding burnout:

1. Set limits: Set limits on the amount of time you spend consuming news and social media each day. It's essential to take breaks to avoid burnout and maintain a healthy balance.

2. Stay organized: Organize the sources and topics you follow by priority, and don't hesitate to unsubscribe from sources that don't add value.

3. Curate your feeds: Apply importance to specific subjects, people, or publications that you trust and regularly curate the feeds that you follow.

4. Revisit sources: Regularly revisit and review the sources you trust to make sure they are still reliable, as sources' accuracy or depth can change over time.

5. Be open-minded: Try to explore different perspectives on issues and topics, even those you don't agree with. It can expand your knowledge and understanding of things and provide a more balanced view.

6. Take care of yourself: Remember to prioritize self-care, exercise, and do things that you enjoy outside of news and social media.

Remember, keeping up with every piece of information can be challenging, and it's okay to take breaks and focus on your well-being. It's important to set boundaries, prioritize reliable sources, and practice mindfulness.
<!-- SOURCE_TURN_009_END -->
